title: The Serpent’s Breath: Escape from Chichén Itzá
description: A tougher field version where physics relationships matter more and wrong paths cost serious oxygen.

answerKey.method: Escape route unlocked by translating carvings and applying physics: light/shadow, balance, airflow, echo timing, and astronomy alignment.
answerKey.motive: The temple was built as a trial of knowledge: only someone who respects the writings, sculptures, and laws of nature can leave safely.
answerKey.keyEvidence: The serpent glyph warns that fire reveals truth but steals breath; airflow and echo clues point away from dead-end tunnels; the final star-serpent alignment opens the oxygen gate.
answerKey.explanation: Solve light angle, torque balance, echo timing, and airflow together; the safest exit is the southeast current after the raised-torch serpent alignment.

openingNarration: You are Dr. Reyes, a Latin American archaeologist called to Chichén Itzá after ground-penetrating scans revealed a sealed chamber beneath the old stone complex. For years you studied how Mayan builders used sculpture, astronomy, mathematics, and writing to preserve knowledge. Tonight, the temple answers back. A stone door drops behind you. Your oxygen monitor flashes: 30 minutes of usable air. A torch rests beside the entry. It can reveal hidden carvings, but every second of flame burns oxygen faster. The walls, floor, and ceiling are covered in ancient symbols. They are not decoration. They are instructions. Translate them, trust the physics, choose the correct paths, and escape before the Serpent’s Breath runs out. This session is Level 3: Field Archaeologist. Wrong choices add 60 seconds of oxygen loss.
revealScript: Level 3: Field Archaeologist complete. The fastest safe escape required oxygen discipline, Mayan symbol translation, physics reasoning, and the final route: Solve light angle, torque balance, echo timing, and airflow together; the safest exit is the southeast current after the raised-torch serpent alignment.

publicClues.title: Oxygen Warning
publicClues.text: Thirty minutes of usable oxygen remain. Extra heat accelerates oxygen loss.

publicClues.title: Torch Glyph
publicClues.text: The serpent’s painted body appears only when light hits from a low angle.

publicClues.title: Tunnel Evidence
publicClues.text: A long echo means distance or a dangerous hollow. Moving air means connection.

publicClues.title: Balance Room
publicClues.text: Torque matters: force multiplied by distance. Equal mass is not always balance.

publicClues.title: Ceiling Map
publicClues.text: The torch angle changes the pointer. A higher flame moves the serpent eye toward the star.

publicClues.title: Final Oxygen Gate
publicClues.text: The final lock opens only when translation and physics agree.

casefeed.title: Level 3: Field Archaeologist Entry Log
casefeed.text: Dr. Reyes enters the hidden chamber. This is Field Archaeologist: A tougher field version where physics relationships matter more and wrong paths cost serious oxygen.

casefeed.title: Translation Note
casefeed.text: Mayan inscriptions often combine image, sound, and meaning. Read sculpture placement, not just symbols.

casefeed.title: Temple Physics Warning
casefeed.text: The chamber is designed around light, air, weight, and echo. Wrong turns waste oxygen; careful observation saves it.

phone.title: Oxygen Monitor
phone.text: O₂ Reserve: 30 minutes. Wrong checkpoint/path choices add 60 seconds. Torch flame doubles oxygen drain while active.

phone.title: Sensor Flicker
phone.text: Air current detected from the east-facing passage. Still air detected from the north passage.

messages.title: Field Team Message
messages.text: Comms are weak. Remember: Chichén Itzá builders aligned structures with sky events. Check walls and ceilings together.

messages.title: Final Warning From Surface
messages.text: Your oxygen telemetry is dropping. Use the torch only when reading carvings or casting alignment shadows.

maps.title: Temple Sketch
maps.text: Chamber layout: Descent Hall → Shadow Wall → Balance Room → Three Paths → Oxygen Gate.

maps.title: Path Choice
maps.text: Draft moves toward the southeast tunnel. The quiet north tunnel has no dust disturbance and no oxygen movement.

photos.title: Torch-Revealed Pigment
photos.text: A faded blue-green pigment appears only in torchlight, forming a serpent body pointing toward a wall niche.

photos.title: Serpent Shadow
photos.text: When the torch is low, the serpent head shadow misses the ceiling star. When raised to shoulder height, the eye nearly aligns.

contacts.title: Mentor Note: Dr. Itzel Cocom
contacts.text: The writing is a system. Floor carvings often mark danger, wall carvings give instruction, ceiling carvings reveal timing or alignment.

notes.title: Symbol Glossary Fragment
notes.text: Breath = moving air. Serpent = path or test. Flame = revealed truth and consumed oxygen. Closed eye = dead end. Difficulty note: Field Archaeologist reduces how obvious the safest route feels.

notes.title: Balance Ratio
notes.text: Jade appears twice, maize once, jaguar three times. The floor scale expects a 2:1:3 relationship.

files.title: Physics Field Sheet
files.text: Echo timing clue: shorter echo usually means a shorter chamber or blocked path; moving air suggests connection to an opening or vent.

files.title: Lever Notes
files.text: A balanced lever has equal torque on both sides: force multiplied by distance. Heavier stones can balance lighter stones placed farther away.

browser.title: Chichén Itzá Research Cache
browser.text: The site is associated with astronomy, architecture, carved serpent imagery, and ceremonial movement through space.

browser.title: Shadow Alignment Reminder
browser.text: A shadow can act like a pointer. Move the light source, not the wall, to change the shadow angle.

questions.prompt: What is the safest way to use the torch in this oxygen-limited chamber?

options.label: Use short bursts only when reading carvings or casting shadows.
Leave it on for the entire run.
Never use it, even when symbols are hidden.
Wave it randomly to scare the temple.

questions.prompt: The serpent carving is visible but incomplete until the torch casts a shadow. What matters most?

options.label: The largest visible doorway.
The shadow alignment created by torch angle and carving.
The dustiest tunnel.
The quiet passage with no airflow.

questions.prompt: The balance room gives a ratio and a lever. Which physics idea should guide the choice?

options.label: All objects weigh the same on ancient stone.
The heaviest stone always wins.
Balance depends on ratio, mass, and distance from the pivot.
A lever works only when no force is applied.

questions.prompt: Three tunnel mouths appear. Which evidence best suggests a living escape route?

options.label: No airflow and a closed-eye glyph.
The longest echo and the heaviest dust.
The tunnel that looks easiest without reading symbols.
Moving airflow with matching serpent/breath markings.

questions.prompt: The final seal repeats Breath, Shadow, and Current. What should the archaeologist do?

options.label: Use moving air, brief torchlight, and serpent-shadow alignment together.
Burn the torch continuously until oxygen is gone.
Pick the quiet mouth because it feels calm.
Ignore the ceiling and follow only the floor.

questions.prompt: What is the safest final route out of the temple?

options.label: North tunnel, closed-eye glyph, no airflow.
Left tunnel, deepest echo, heavy dust.
Southeast airflow tunnel after aligning the serpent eye shadow.
Any tunnel after turning the torch off forever.
A literal monster breathing fire.
The limited moving air and knowledge trail that marks the living path.
A command to run without thinking.
A warning to avoid all physics clues.

questions.prompt: Which strategy gives the fastest escape?

options.label: Keep the torch on and inspect everything slowly.
Choose paths quickly without reading.
Use every hint before observing.
Use short torch bursts, translate key symbols, and trust physics clues.
